# 1 Enoch Chapter 40 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS | **Section:** Book of Parables

---

**40:1** And after that I saw thousands upon thousands and ten thousand upon ten thousand — a multitude beyond number and reckoning — standing before the glory of the Lord of Spirits.

**40:2** And on the four wings of the Lord of Spirits I saw four presences, different from those who stand without sleeping. I learned their names, for the angel who accompanied me made known their names to me and showed me all hidden things.

**40:3** And I heard the voices of those four presences as they uttered praises before the Lord of glory.

**40:4** The first voice blesses the Lord of Spirits forever and ever.

**40:5** The second voice I heard blessing the Elect One and the elect ones who depend upon the Lord of Spirits.

**40:6** The third voice I heard petitioning and praying on behalf of those who dwell on the dry ground and supplicating in the name of the Lord of Spirits.

**40:7** The fourth voice I heard driving away the adversaries and forbidding them to come before the Lord of Spirits to accuse those who dwell on the dry ground.

**40:8** After that I asked the angel of peace who accompanied me and showed me all hidden things: "Who are these four presences which I have seen and whose words I have heard and written down?"

**40:9** And he said to me: "The first is Michael, the merciful and long-suffering; the second, who is set over all the diseases and all the wounds of the children of men, is Raphael; the third, who is set over all the powers, is Gabriel; and the fourth, who is set over the works of repentance and the hope of those who inherit eternal life, is named Phanuel."

**40:10** These are the four angels of the Lord of Spirits and the four voices I heard in those days.

---

*LOGOS notes: The four archangels are here assigned distinct liturgical and cosmic functions. Phanuel's domain — repentance and eternal hope — is not attested elsewhere in Jewish literature outside 1 Enoch. "Angel of peace" is the guide figure accompanying Enoch throughout the Parables.*
